title: Ops Mentorship Rotation Brief — week of 2026-11-02
content:
Purpose
Quick operational debrief and mentoring notes for the rotation that started 2026-11-02. This doc combines the week's standup snippets, incident sketches, SLO snapshots, and coaching action items for newer on-call engineers. Use this in 1:1s and handoffs.

Summary highlights (TL;DR)
- One moderately impacting latency incident on 2026-11-01 (early morning UTC) that touched hosted-api -> model-routing path; mitigated with a temporary routing rule and kv-cache policy rollback.
- p95 token-gen latency for hosted-api routes increased above target for a 30-minute window; error budget usage +11% this sprint.
- Several small on-call learning moments: triage playbook gaps (observability link names), missing runbook step for warm-starting dedicated pools.
- Action items assigned for playbook cleanup, automated smoke test for routing changes, and a coaching session scheduled for new joiners.

Standup notes (snippets collected across the week)
- Mon 11/02 morning: "Observed slight tail-latency bump on us-west-2; spike coincided with large batch reruns from a customer test job. Scaling responded but KV cache thrash visible." — Marco
- Tue 11/03 handoff: "Triggered fallback to model-variant-2 for a handful of routes; customer impact minimal but flagged for RCA." — Lena
- Wed 11/04 mid-day: "Confirmed root cause looks like cache eviction policy change in v1.9.3 - probabilistic TTL combo with large sequence lengths." — Ravi
- Thu 11/05 retro: "Good cross-team comms; metrics links were helpful but a couple of step names in the playbook caused confusion (see TODO below)." — Aisha

Incident sketch: latency-throttle-2026-11-01
- Start: 2026-11-01 03:14 UTC; End: 2026-11-01 03:46 UTC
- Affected: hosted-api (text generation endpoints), primarily model-routing layer between proxy and serving runtime.
- Symptoms: p95 token latency rose from baseline ~220ms to ~1.4s; a small increase in 5xxs for long-sequence requests.
- Immediate mitigation: temporarily pinned routing policy to variant-2 for affected routes at 03:20 UTC; scaled dedicated serving pool by +20% while rollback prepared.
- Root cause hypothesis: rollout of kv-cache TTL change in infra release v1.9.3 created eviction storms when combined with a customer batch job with long context lengths. The change reduced cached prefix retention unexpectedly.
- Post-incident actions: create a dedicated smoke test (see action A1), add an automated detection rule for KV eviction rate (A2), update canary rollout checklist to include long-context workload test (A3).
- Owners: A1 -> Marco; A2 -> Ravi; A3 -> Lena

SLO snapshot (quick numbers for oncall reference)
- Hosted API text-generation: latency p95 target: 300ms (rolling 30d) — this week: 330ms (30-min breach window contributed 11% error budget).
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly — no hard availability breach this week; transient 4xx rise observed (customer retries).
- Error budget remaining (month-to-date): ~88.7% (approx).
- Note: two related metrics to watch during rollouts: kv_cache_eviction_rate and routing_requeue_rate. Both spiked during the incident.

On-call handoffs and mentoring notes
- Handoff cadence this rotation:
  - Night shift (UTC): Ravi (2026-11-02 22:00 UTC -> 2026-11-03 08:00 UTC)
  - Day shift: Marco (2026-11-03 08:00 UTC -> 2026-11-04 18:00 UTC)
  - Swing: Lena (2026-11-04 18:00 UTC -> 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC)
- Coaching reminders for new oncall engineers:
  1) Early triage checklist: check SLO dashboards, then routing metrics, then KV cache graphs, then recent infra deploys. Don’t escalate immediately — collect 3 signals.
  2) When running mitigations (fallbacks/variant pinning), always annotate the routing rule with a link to the incident ticket and set an automatic 1-hour revert timer if it's a temporary pin.
  3) Escalation thresholds: if p95 > 800ms for >10min or >0.5% 5xx rate for >5min, page senior oncall (level-2).
  4) Communication template: short status line, impact estimation (users affected / endpoints), mitigation in-progress, action owner and ETA. Post a first update within 8 minutes of paging.

Playbook updates (items to merge into Confluence)
- Rename step "check caches" to "check kv_cache_eviction_rate and prefix_hit_ratio" (confusing before). — TODO (A4)
- Add warm-start checklist for dedicated pools (how to pre-warm GPU memory and KV cache) — TODO (A5)
- Insert a canary test case that submits a long-context batch (50k tokens) and validates routing stability under load — TODO (A3)
- Add a short troubleshooting flow for model-variant mismatches and demo script for safe rollback — TODO (A6)

Follow-ups and owners (quick list)
- A1: infra smoke test for routing + long-context: Marco — due 2026-11-12
- A2: alert for kv_cache_eviction_rate > baseline*3: Ravi — due 2026-11-09
- A3: canary checklist addition + test case: Lena — due 2026-11-10
- A4: playbook step rename + doc cleanup: Aisha — due 2026-11-08
- A5: warm-start dedicated pool runbook: Platform Eng (assign slack @platform-oncall) — due 2026-11-15
- A6: rollback demo + runbook snippet: Marco + DevEx — due 2026-11-14

Open questions / discussion points
- Should we gate the KV TTL change behind a stricter canary policy that includes long-context customers? Pros/cons for deployment velocity vs risk.
- Is our current error budget policy for p95 aligned with PL product expectations? Customer-facing contracts might need a different SLA lane.
- Can we automate the fallback-to-variant mechanism so it’s a low-friction self-heal instead of a manual pin? (security/consistency concerns).

Notes to self (informal)
- Patch for visibility: add direct links to runbook sections inside the alert pages so oncall can click-through from the pager.
- Quick reminder: remember to include the incident timeline in the Jira ticket before closing (timestamps matter!).

Slack refs and files observed during week
- #sre-oncall: thread CB12345 (linked above) — contains raw command outputs and ephemeral logs we used during mitigation.
- Incident ticket: JIRA-SRE-4532 (RCA in progress; draft attached in ticket comments)
- PR for temporary revert: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287 (revert of kv-ttl commit)

Closing note
Thanks to the rotation crew for quick coordination and clear comms. The coaching focus for the next rotation will be: runbook fluency, faster hypothesis formation (collect the 3 signals faster), and practicing safe rollbacks in staging. We'll review progress in next week's handoff.

Aisha (oncall lead)
